{{Short description|American mathematician, born 1946}}
'''Glenn Shafer''' (born November 21, 1946) is an American mathematician and statistician. He is the co-creator of [[Dempster–Shafer theory]]. He is a university professor and a board of governors professor at [[Rutgers University]], as well as a former dean of its [[Rutgers Business School – Newark and New Brunswick|business school]].

== Early life and education ==

Shafer grew up on a farm near [[Caney, Kansas]]. He earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Princeton University]], then entered the [[Peace Corps]], serving in Afghanistan. He returned to Princeton, earning a PhD in mathematical statistics in 1973 under [[Geoffrey Watson]].<ref name="faculty">{{cite web|url=http://www.business.rutgers.edu/faculty/glenn-shafer|title=Glenn Shafer|work=Rutgers University|accessdate=12 June 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612232742/http://www.business.rutgers.edu/faculty/glenn-shafer|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Glenn Shafer |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=100562 |website=[[The Mathematics Genealogy Project]] |access-date=13 July 2022 |archive-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220522013441/https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=100562 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Career ==
Shafer taught at Princeton and the [[University of Kansas]], joining the faculty of [[Rutgers Business School – Newark and New Brunswick]] in 1992. From 2011 to 2014, he served as dean of the business school of the university.

During the 1970s and 1980s Shafer expanded a theory first introduced by the Harvard professor, [[Arthur P. Dempster]], to create [[Dempster–Shafer theory]], also described as, the theory of belief functions or evidence theory. It is a general framework for reasoning with uncertainty, allowing one to combine evidence from different sources and to arrive at a degree of belief (represented by a mathematical object called ''belief function'') that takes into account all the available evidence.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Fine, Terrence L.|authorlink=Terrence L. Fine|title=Review: Glenn Shafer, ''A mathematical theory of evidence''|journal=[[Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.]]|year=1977|volume=83|issue=4|pages=667–672|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183538896|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1977-14338-3|doi-access=free|access-date=2018-06-12|archive-date=2018-06-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613014815/https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183538896|url-status=live}}</ref> The theory and its extensions have been of particular interest to the [[artificial intelligence]] community.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Zadeh|first=L. A.|authorlink=Lotfi Zadeh|year=1984|title=Review of A Mathematical Theory of Evidence (PDF)|journal=AI Magazine|volume=5|issue=3|url=https://www.aaai.org/ojs/index.php/aimagazine/article/download/452/388|access-date=2018-06-12|archive-date=2015-10-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019034833/http://www.aaai.org/ojs/index.php/aimagazine/article/download/452/388|url-status=live}}</ref>

More recently Shafer worked with [[Vladimir Vovk]] to develop a [[game theory|game-theoretic]] framework for [[probability]]. That work produced a 2001 book, ''Probability and Finance: It's Only a Game!''. A joint research group between Rutgers and [[Royal Holloway|Royal Holloway, University of London]] has produced more than 50 working papers on the subject.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.probabilityandfinance.com/|title=The Game-Theoretic Probability and Finance Project|work=Probability and Finance|accessdate=12 June 2018|archive-date=24 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624082942/http://www.probabilityandfinance.com/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Principal publications ===
* Shafer, Glenn, ''A Mathematical Theory of Evidence'', Princeton University Press, 1976.<ref>Shafer, Glenn; ''A Mathematical Theory of Evidence'', Princeton University Press, 1976, {{ISBN|0-608-02508-9}}</ref> 
* Shafer, Glenn, and Vovk, Vladimir, ''Probability and Finance: It's Only a Game!'', John Wiley and Sons, 2001.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Shafer|first1=Glenn|last2=Vovk|first2=Vladimir|title=Probability and Finance: It's Only a Game!|year=2001|publisher=Wiley Series in Probability and Statistics|isbn=978-0471402268}}</ref>
* Shafer, Glenn, and Vovk, Vladimir, ''Game‐Theoretic Foundations for Probability and Finance'', John Wiley and Sons, 2019.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Shafer|first1=Glenn|last2=Vovk|first2=Vladimir|title=Game‐Theoretic Foundations for Probability and Finance|year=2019|publisher=Wiley Series in Probability and Statistics|isbn=9780470903056}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
Shafer is designated as a Board of Governors Professor at Rutgers. The [[Prague University of Economics and Business]] recognized him with an honorary doctorate in 2009<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-10-08 |title=The VŠE awarded A. P. Dempster and G. Shafer honorary doctorate |url=https://www.vse.cz/english/press-releases/the-vse-awarded-a-p-dempster-and-g-shafer-honorary-doctorate/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-09-08}}</ref>. He has been a [[Fulbright Fellow]] and a [[Guggenheim Fellow]].<ref name = "faculty"/> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence]] in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elected AAAI Fellows |url=https://aaai.org/about-aaai/aaai-awards/the-aaai-fellows-program/elected-aaai-fellows/ |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=AAAI |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129223333/https://aaai.org/about-aaai/aaai-awards/the-aaai-fellows-program/elected-aaai-fellows/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life ==

He is married to retired Princeton history professor, author, and artist [[Nell Irvin Painter]].
